learnables.predictableError: the nominative plural is IDENTICAL to the singular — 'en moški' / 'trije moški' — so only the numeral tells you how many; and the same word is also the adjective 'male'
confusing 'ženska' (a woman) with 'žena' (a wife); the accusative is 'žensko'
the plural is irregular — 'dva otroka', 'trije otroci', and the genitive plural is the bare 'pet otrok'; never 'otroki'
'moj fant' means 'my boyfriend', not 'my boy' — for a son say 'sin'; animate, so the accusative is 'fanta'
'dekle' is neuter despite meaning a female — 'lepo dekle', 'to dekle', 'mlado dekle', never 'lepa dekle'
after a number from five up it goes genitive plural 'ljudi' — 'pet ljudi', 'koliko ljudi' — while 3 and 4 take the masculine 'trije/štirje ljudje'
'oseba' is always feminine even about a man — 'ena oseba', 'dve osebi', 'pet oseb'; never 'dva oseba'
'družina' is feminine — 'moja družina je velika' — and it takes the accusative as an object: 'Imam veliko družino.' Beware 'družina' is the family unit; relatives more broadly are 'sorodniki'.
the adjective agrees with what it describes — 'mlad moški', 'mlada ženska', 'mlado dekle' — English speakers leave it frozen as 'mlad'

learnables.gloss: old (of a person or a thing)
learnables.predictableError: the same word does double duty — 'star moški' (an old man) and 'Star sem 30 let' (age); as a describing word it must agree: 'stara ženska', 'staro mesto'

learnables.gloss: tall (of a person); high (of a thing)
learnables.predictableError: one word covers both English 'tall' and 'high', and it agrees — 'visoka ženska', 'visoko drevo'
the fleeting -e- drops the moment it inflects — 'majhna soba', 'majhno stanovanje', 'majhni otroci' — not 'majhena'
agreement — 'vesela ženska', 'veseli otroci'; 'vesel' is the cheer you can see in a picture, while 'srečen' is the deeper 'fortunate/happy'
'lep' agrees as an adjective ('lepa hiša', 'lepo mesto'), while 'lepo' as a standalone is the adverb ('lepo poje')
agreement — 'velika hiša', 'veliko stanovanje'; and beware that neuter-looking 'veliko' separately means 'a lot of' + genitive ('veliko ljudi')

one form covers both English tenses — 'dela' is 'he works' and 'he is working', so there is no auxiliary to add; the slip is answering 'Kaj dela?' with the 1sg 'delam', or reaching for 'deluje', which is 'functions/operates', not 'works for a living'
'talking WITH someone' is 'z' + instrumental — 'govori z ženo', not 'govori s žena'; the language is an adverb ('govori slovensko')

learnables.gloss: to eat — 3sg 'je' (he/she eats), identical in form to 'je' = is
learnables.predictableError: the 3sg 'je' is spelt exactly like 'je' = is — only the accusative object separates them ('Moški je sendvič.' = the man is EATING a sandwich; in careful writing you will see it marked 'jé'). The 3pl is the irregular 'jedo'.
the drink goes accusative — 'pije kavo', not 'pije kava'; 3pl is 'pijejo'
for an action in progress you need the imperfective 'kupuje'; the perfective 'kupi' means 'buys/will buy' the once, so a picture is always 'kupuje'
'waiting for' is 'na' + accusative or nothing at all — 'čaka na avtobus' / 'čaka avtobus' — never the English-shaped 'čaka za avtobus'
'sedi' is the state of sitting; sitting DOWN is the different verb 'usede se'. Where they sit is locative — 'sedi na klopi', 'sedi v kavarni'
Slovene has two verbs spelt 'stati' — this one gives 'stoji' (stands), the other gives 'stane' (costs); they are not forms of one word
the dish goes accusative — 'kuha juho'; and note 'kuha kavo' is how Slovene says 'makes coffee'
no preposition and an accusative object — 'gleda televizijo', 'gleda otroke', not 'gleda na televizijo'

learnables.gloss: the two of them are talking / chatting (to each other) — dual
learnables.predictableError: exactly two people take the DUAL 'pogovarjata se'; three or more take 'pogovarjajo se'. The reflexive 'se' can never be dropped, and it never comes first — it is a second-position clitic ('Pogovarjata se.', 'Dva moška se pogovarjata.').

learnables.gloss: three / four people (the masculine-plural numeral forms)
learnables.predictableError: masculine 3 and 4 have their own shapes — 'trije ljudje', 'štirje moški' — not the neuter/feminine 'tri'/'štiri'; from five up it flips to the genitive plural, 'pet ljudi'
the dual, not the plural — 'dve osebi', never 'dve osebe'; and 'oseba' is feminine, so it is 'dve', never 'dva'
being there is locative 'v banki'; going there is accusative 'v banko' — the -i/-o ending is the whole difference
the post office takes 'na', not 'v' — 'na pošti' (at), 'na pošto' (to)
'v trgovini' (in the shop) vs 'v trgovino' (to the shop); the activity of shopping is the separate word 'nakupovanje'
'v lekarni' / 'v lekarno'; a 'drogerija' is a toiletries shop and does not dispense medicine
it is masculine even though it ends in -o — 'v kino' (to the cinema), 'v kinu' (at the cinema); not neuter 'v kinem'
the market takes 'na' — 'na tržnici' (at), 'na tržnico' (to) — never 'v tržnici'
'v hotelu' (at the hotel, locative) vs 'v hotel' (to the hotel); inanimate, so the accusative equals the nominative
it takes 'na' — 'na postaji' (at the stop), 'na postajo' (to the stop); and 'do postaje' is genitive after 'do'
'v šoli' (at school) vs 'v šolo' (to school); Slovene uses no article, so it is just 'grem v šolo'

learnables.gloss: in / at ___ — where something IS: locative ('v trgovini', 'na pošti')
learnables.predictableError: location takes the LOCATIVE ('v trgovini', 'na pošti'), while motion towards takes the accusative ('grem v trgovino') — and which preposition is lexical: 'v banki / v trgovini / v šoli' but 'na pošti / na tržnici / na postaji'
'doma' already means 'at home' — no preposition ('Sem doma', never 'v doma'); going home is the separate word 'domov'
'zunaj' is being outside; going out is 'ven' — 'Otroci so zunaj' vs 'Gremo ven'
'v mestu' (in town) — locative, neuter; and watch the second sense, 'prosto mesto' is a free SPOT, not a free city
an address takes 'na' + locative and the street name is an adjective that agrees — 'na Slovenski ulici', not 'na Slovenska ulica'
neuter locative after 'v' — 'Živim v stanovanju', not 'v stanovanji' or 'v stanovanje'
'v hiši' (in the house); a 'hiša' is a whole detached house — the flat you rent in a building is 'stanovanje', not 'hiša'
'v sobi' (locative); 'soba' alone is just 'a room' — a living room is 'dnevna soba' and a bedroom is 'spalnica'
locative after 'v' — 'v kuhinji', not 'v kuhinja'
'kopalnica' is where you wash; the toilet is 'stranišče' and in Slovene flats it is often a separate room — asking for the 'kopalnica' in a bar gets you a puzzled look
'v bloku' (locative) is the building; your own flat inside it is still 'stanovanje' — the two are not interchangeable
the bare nominative only works as a subject — it is 'v Sloveniji' (locative) for 'in Slovenia' and 'iz Slovenije' (genitive) for 'from Slovenia'
genitive after 'iz' — 'Sem iz Anglije', not 'iz Anglija'; and 'Anglija' is England only, the UK is 'Velika Britanija'
'iz Amerike' (genitive), 'v Ameriki' (locative); everyday Slovene says 'Amerika' where the official name is 'Združene države'
'iz Nemčije' / 'v Nemčiji'; the nationality is 'Nemec / Nemka' and the language is the adverb 'nemško'
'iz Italije' / 'v Italiji'; the nationality is 'Italijan / Italijanka'
Croatia takes 'na', not 'v' — 'na Hrvaškem' (in Croatia), 'na Hrvaško' (to Croatia), 's Hrvaške' (from Croatia); it declines like an adjective
spelt with a v — 'Avstrija' — and not to be confused with 'Avstralija'; 'iz Avstrije' / 'v Avstriji'
the nationality is a capitalised NOUN with its own feminine form — a woman says 'Angležinja' — and it takes no preposition: 'Sem Anglež' but 'Sem iz Anglije'

'rad' takes a FINITE verb, not an infinitive — 'Rad berem', 'Rada kuham', never 'rad brati'; and this is not 'rad bi', which is a one-off wish ('I'd like'), so dropping or adding 'bi' changes the meaning entirely
the plural is 'hobiji' ('moji hobiji so …'); in speech Slovenes far more often open with 'V prostem času …' than with 'Moj hobi je …'
'doing sport' is the reflexive verb + instrumental — 'ukvarjam se s športom' — never the calque 'delam šport'
accusative object — 'poslušam glasbo', not 'poslušam glasba'; 'muzika' is a loose colloquialism, 'glasba' is the word
the natural spoken line is the verb — 'Rad berem' — with the noun 'branje' kept for listing; and it is neuter ('branje me veseli')
same as 'branje' — say 'Rada kuham' rather than 'Moj hobi je kuhanje'; the noun is neuter
'go for a walk' is 'grem na sprehod' — 'na' + accusative — not 'za sprehod' or 'v sprehod'
'žena' is specifically a WIFE — a woman in general is 'ženska'; accusative 'ženo', instrumental 'z ženo'
'mož' is specifically a HUSBAND — a man in general is 'moški'; it is animate, so the accusative is 'moža' ('imam moža')
animate masculine — 'imam sina', not 'imam sin'; the plural is the irregular 'sinovi'
it declines off a different stem — accusative 'hčer', plural 'hčere' — and in everyday Ljubljana speech people mostly just say 'hčerka'
animate — 'imam brata', not 'imam brat'; the plural is the irregular 'bratje'
accusative 'sestro'; the counted forms are 'dve sestri' (dual) and the genitive plural 'pet sester'
gender — a man says 'poročen', a woman 'poročena'; 'married TO someone' is 'poročen z' + instrumental, and the opposite is 'samski / samska'

learnables.gloss: compound numerals 21–99: the UNIT first, then -in-, then the whole tens word, all as one word — shown here on the 20s and 30s, and the same rule runs to 99 (enaindvajset 21, petintrideset 35, devetindevetdeset 99)
learnables.predictableError: English order — saying the tens first ('dvajset ena'). Slovene puts the UNIT first and glues it on with -in- to the full tens word, all as ONE written word: 21 = ena+in+dvajset 'enaindvajset', 35 'petintrideset', 45 'petinštirideset', 99 'devetindevetdeset'.
the Listening paper's three-way trap — 'dvanajst' (12), 'enaindvajset' (21), 'trideset' (30); 21 is built on 'dvajset', so its ending sounds nothing like the teen's '-najst'
'konec' takes the GENITIVE — 'konec tedna', never 'konec teden'; 'at the weekend' is 'ob koncu tedna' (locative), and this is the form you meet on signs and in print, not in the bar
